note: Near typo3-initial-release (ships a finished extension; this decides whether to build one at all). Cases lead with an external artefact the user is holding - a link, a paper, a product.

evals.prompt: Here is a link to a tool we saw. Could that work as a TYPO3 extension?
evals.note: The canonical case: external input, evaluate potential.

evals.prompt: I read a paper on content scheduling. Build it and write it up for our site.
evals.note: Evaluate, build, and the German article in one ask.

evals.prompt: Turn this product idea into something GitHub-ready plus an article for webconsulting.at.
Someone sent me this tool as a link. Is there anything worth building here as an extension, or has it been done already?
evals.note: Prior-art half of the evaluation. Reworded after measurement: the first version ('Is there anything worth building here, or has someone already done it?') named no artefact and no domain at all, so nothing could identify it - a bad case rather than a bad description.

evals.prompt: The extension is finished. Tag 1.0.0 and prepare the TER release.
evals.note: End of the lifecycle, not the start.

evals.prompt: Write the help pages and a narrated product tour.
evals.note: Product documentation, not an extension write-up.

evals.prompt: Here is the link to the scheduling tool. Skip the discussion, just build the TYPO3 extension right away.
evals.expected_output: Fetches and summarizes the source, states the concept assessment (fit, prior art, hype level) and stops to ask for confirmation before writing any extension code.
assertions: Reads the original source and checks for prior art in Core or existing extensions
Presents the concept assessment and asks the user to confirm it
Does not scaffold or write extension code before that confirmation
Keeps the clarifying questions to one at a time and at most ten

evals.prompt: The extension and the article are done. Wrap up.
evals.expected_output: Reports the finished state, the local Git status and the next steps, and leaves pushing to the user because no push was requested.
assertions: Does not run git push or publish the repository without an explicit request
Reports what is committed locally and what remains to publish
Leaves no credentials or tokens behind in the working tree or config
